supported_feature_keys.promotion_evidence: RFC-0108 Slice 0 added platform analytics UI observability contract validation, generated-app product-safe error scaffolding, structured JSON event logging, supported-features placeholders, RFC evidence scaffolding, operations documentation, API certification documentation, and generated scaffold tests.

RFC-0108 Slice 2 adds the governed analytics UI telemetry contract for browser events, gateway log events, severity levels, attention event types, audit event types, trace attributes, dashboard/alert reference policy, protected diagnostics policy, and validator tests without emitting runtime telemetry.

RFC-0108 Slice 9 adds a machine-readable rollout-readiness contract, validator, and unit tests that tie certified Workbench route/panel scope to Slice 8 proof, separate planned residual scope, and prove validators reject forbidden labels and unimplemented metric references.

RFC-0108 second-last slice adds a machine-readable hardening review contract, validator, and tests covering telemetry fields, panel states, API/Swagger applicability, dashboard and alert certification, enterprise governance, residual planned scope, and no open P0/P1 findings before closure.

RFC-0108 Slice 3 adds Workbench analytics UI correlation helpers, client-side BFF request headers, BFF proxy correlation/trace generation and malformed traceparent replacement tests, while keeping correlation and trace identifiers out of metric labels.

RFC-0108 Slice 1 adds code-owned Workbench analytics UI observability vocabulary and tests for allowed labels, forbidden sensitive fields, state vocabulary, and planned Workbench metric-family names without emitting product telemetry.

RFC-0108 Slice 5 adds Workbench local analytics UI metric events and tests for ready, empty, partial, stale, degraded, error, permission-blocked, unsupported, API duration, panel state, panel hydration, and sensitive-field exclusion.
Source-backed freshness/supportability contract proof and browser validation remain planned until backend-owned freshness and supportability metrics exist.

RFC-0108 Slice 5 adds a platform Grafana dashboard artifact and Prometheus alert rules that reference only implemented Workbench metric-family names, with validator and unit coverage rejecting unimplemented metric references and forbidden dashboard/alert content.

RFC-0108 Slice 6 adds Workbench attention events and an attention counter for stale, degraded, partial-source, and repeated-failure selected analytics panel states, with deduplication, bounded severity, source-backed reason codes, and sensitive-field exclusion tests.

RFC-0108 Slice 7 adds Gateway product-safe analytics read audit logs for selected Workbench performance and risk analytics reads. Successful upstream reads emit analytics_read_allowed, 401/403 upstream denials emit analytics_read_denied, and tests prove bounded audit fields plus exclusion of portfolio, client, request, response, and raw entitlement failure content. Protected diagnostics lookup audit remains planned until a protected diagnostics API exists.

RFC-0108 Slice 8 adds platform-owned canonical proof review and live governed Workbench evidence for PB_SG_GLOBAL_BAL_001. The proof bundle records API checks, calculation sanity checks, panel classifications, browser screenshots, dashboard/alert metric reconciliation, Workbench /api/metrics family exposure, and sensitive-content assertions while leaving gateway/backend metrics, protected diagnostics lookup audit, and full caller-context entitlement certification planned.
Fan-out metric tests, dashboard reconciliation, and OpenAPI/API certification evidence where API shape changes.

RFC-0108 Slice 4 emits product-safe structured gateway fan-out logs for selected Workbench performance and risk analytics operations with route, service, operation, state, supportability, status class, bounded reason, and no sensitive request/response payload fields.

RFC-0108 Slice 3 proves Gateway middleware accepts valid traceparent, rejects malformed traceparent, emits safe response trace headers, and forwards correlation and trace context to analytics backend clients without adding sensitive labels.

RFC-0108 Slice 1 adds code-owned Gateway analytics UI observability vocabulary and tests for allowed labels, forbidden sensitive fields, state vocabulary, and planned Gateway metric-family names without emitting fan-out metrics.
